{{nihongo|'''Isasumi Shrine'''|伊佐須美神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].

[[File:Isasumi-jinja torii.JPG|thumb|250px|right|{{Center|Torii}}]]'''Isasumi Shrine'' (Isasumi Shrine) is located in {{ill|Fukushima Prefecture|Q71707|qid=Q71707}}{{ill|Ōnuma District|ceb|Ōnuma-gun|fa|شهرستان اونوما، فوکوشیما|fr|District d'Ōnuma|id|Distrik Ōnuma, Fukushima|it|Distretto di Ōnuma|ja|大沼郡|ko|오누마군|nl|Onuma (district)|pl|Powiat Ōnuma|ru|Онума (уезд)|sco|Ōnuma Destrict|uk|Повіт Онума|zh|大沼郡|zh_yue|大沼郡|qid=Q1155853}}{{ill|Aizumisato|arz|ايزوميساتو|ceb|Aizu-misato Machi|es|Aizumisato (Fukushima)|fa|ایزومیساتو، فوکوشیما|fr|Aizumisato|id|Aizumisato, Fukushima|it|Aizumisato|ja|会津美里町|ko|아이즈미사토정|ms|Aizumisato, Fukushima|my|အအိဇုမိဆတိုမြို့|pl|Aizumisato|pt|Aizumisato|ru|Айдзумисато|sv|Aizumisato|tl|Aizumisato, Fukushima|tr|Aizumisato|uk|Айдзу-Місато|uz|Aizumisato (Fukushima)|vi|Aizumisato, Fukushima|zh|會津美里町|zh_yue|會津美里町|qid=Q1205357}} Miyabayashi. {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}), {{ill|Mutsu Province|Q907389|qid=Q907389}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Ninomiya}}. In the Heisei era, the nation's number one shrine association recognized Ichinomiya as {{ill|Iwashiro Province|Q1370734|qid=Q1370734}}. {{ill|Q712534|lt=old shrine rank}} is {{ill|Kokuhei Chūsha|qid=Q134917280|lt=Kokuheichusha}}, and currently it is {{ill|Beppyo shrine|ja|別表神社|mr|बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|simple|Beppyo shrine|zh|別表神社|qid=Q10898274}} of {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.

=== Overview ===
{{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1993}}, located along the {{ill|Miyagawa|Q11454648|qid=Q11454648|lt=Miyagawa}} on the southern edge of the {{ill|Aizu Basin|Q11381254|qid=Q11381254}}, is the general guardian deity of Ninomiya and Aizu in Mutsu Province. The place name "Aizu" comes from two of the {{ill|Shidō Shōgun|Q9076804|qid=Q9076804}} who were dispatched during the time of the 10th Emperor {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}. 35420|Obiko no Mikoto}} and {{ill|Take Nunokawa Wake no Mikoto|ja|武渟川別|zh|武渟川别|qid=Q11546050|lt=Tatenuma Kawabetsu no Mikoto}}, who traveled on the {{ill|Tōkaidō (region)|Q1196306|qid=Q1196306}}, are said to have met in Aizu, and Isasumi Shrine is said to have been established as the place where the two worshiped the deity to protect the nation. In the Aizu region, large {{ill|Zenpō-kōen-fun|ja|前方後円墳|ko|전방후원분|simple|Zenpō-kōen-fun|zh|前方後圓墳|qid=Q11268718}} unique to the {{ill|Yamato Kingship|Q2658252|qid=Q2658252}} were already built in the early {{ill|Kofun period|Q459939|qid=Q459939}}, and these shrines play an important role in considering the actual situation of the expansion of royal power into the Tohoku region.The precincts are large, and a dense shrine grove spreads out inside. The shrine building was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|2008|Q2004|qid=Q2004}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}}20), so it is currently being rebuilt with a temporary shrine building installed. In addition, as cultural properties, many shrine treasures, natural monuments, and Shinto rituals have been preserved to this day, including the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}} vermilion lacquered gold-bronze mikoshi (national {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}).

=== Enshrined God ===
The following four deities are enshrined {{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine History|1979|p=23}}. It is collectively called ``''Isasumi Okami'''' or ``Isasumi Daimyojin'' {{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1986}}.
:* '''{{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi Mikoto}}''' (Izanagi Mikoto)
:* '''{{ill|Izanami|Q682306|qid=Q682306|lt=Izanami}}''' (Izanami Mikoto)
:* '''{{ill|Ōhiko-no-Mikoto|ja|大彦命|zh|大彦命|qid=Q11435420|lt=Obiko no Mikoto}}''' (Ohiko no Mikoto, Ohiko no Mikoto) - Prince of the 8th {{ill|Emperor Kōgen|Q333572|qid=Q333572}}. He is one of the {{ill|Shidō Shōgun|Q9076804|qid=Q9076804}} and is said to have traveled the {{ill|Hokurikudō|Q3139239|qid=Q3139239}}.
:* '''{{ill|Take Nunokawa Wake no Mikoto|ja|武渟川別|zh|武渟川别|qid=Q11546050|lt=Takenuma Kawabetsu no Mikoto}}''' (Takenuma Kawabetsu no Mikoto, Takenuma Kawabetsu) - Child of Obiko no Mikoto. He is one of the four generals and is said to have traveled the {{ill|Tōkaidō (region)|Q1196306|qid=Q1196306}}.In "{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}, there is one enshrined deity {{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1986}}. In "Isasumi Shrine History" and other current documents, the enshrined deities are described as the above four pillars, but {{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (Shikinai Shrine) | 1986}}{{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (Heibonsha) | 1993}}{{Sfn|Ichinomiya system in medieval countries|2000|pp= 308-309}}, and in addition to the four pillars, two other deities, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shiogama no Okami}} and {{ill|Hachiman|Q261637|qid=Q261637|lt=Hachiman no Okami}}, are enshrined, with Shiogama no Okami on the right and Hachiman on the left. Also, according to "Oshu Ninomiya Eihizan Shoichii Isasumi Taimei Shrine Engi," {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Honjibutsu}} was said to be {{ill|Manjushri|Q471696|qid=Q471696}}{{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1986}}.

=== About the enshrined deity ===
The four deities currently enshrined at Isasumi Shrine are related to the so-called {{ill|Shidō Shōgun|Q9076804|qid=Q9076804}} tale {{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The Shido Shogun is an article written in "{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935}}" <ref group="Hara">'Nihon Shoki', Kogo (9th), September 10th year of Emperor Sujin. It is a general term for the four legendary generals seen in </ref>: {{ill|Ōhiko-no-Mikoto|ja|大彦命|zh|大彦命|qid=Q11435420}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takekawabetsu no Mikoto}}, {{ill|Kibitsuhiko-no-mikoto|Q65318|qid=Q65318}}, and {{ill|Tanba-no-Michinushi-no-Mikoto|Q11368587|qid=Q11368587}}. In the same book, the four people are the October 22nd article of the 10th year of the Emperor Sujin's "Nihon Shoki". In </ref>, he was dispatched to {{ill|Hokurikudō|Q3139239|qid=Q3139239|lt=Hokuriku}}, {{ill|Tōkaidō (region)|Q1196306|qid=Q1196306|lt=Tokai}}, Nishido, and {{ill|Tanba Province|Q954511|qid=Q954511|lt=Tamba}} to pacify the country, and in April 11th year of Emperor Sujin<ref> group="hara">Nihonshoki, April 28th, 11th year of the reign of Emperor Sujin. It is said that the pacification was reported to </ref>. On the other hand, "{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}" <ref group="hara">"Kojiki" Emperor Sujin stage. Although there are differences in who was sent and when, it is said that Obiko no Mikoto and Takenuma Kawabetsu no Mikoto were sent to Takashido and the Twelve Paths of the East, and the origin of the place name is said to be that the place where Obiko no Mikoto and Takenuma Kawabetsu no Mikoto met was named ``Aizu'' (Aizu refers to Aizu).[[File:Kamegamori-kofun zenkei-1.JPG|thumb|230px|right|{{center|{{ill|Kamegamori Kofun|Q132363372|qid=Q132363372}}({{jalin k|Kawanuma District|Q1155856}}{{ill|Aizubange|Q1204988|qid=Q1204988}})}}{{small|The largest tumulus in Aizu, and by extension the second largest in the Tohoku region. }}]]Regarding the story of the Four Paths Shoguns, there are different descriptions in the Kojiki and Nihon Shoki, and the 2nd year of {{ill|Emperor Sushun|Q349238|qid=Q349238}} ({{ill|589|Q31429|qid=Q31429}})<ref group="original">Nihon Shoki, the article on the 1st day of July, 589. Since there is an article in </ref> that appears to indicate that Omi Omimitsu, Shiji Omige, and Abeomi were dispatched as Tosan Doshi, Tokaido envoy, and Hokuriku Doshi, respectively, there is a strong opinion that this is a fabrication based on later events {{Sfn|Hoga|2013|p=19}}. On the other hand, the distribution of the {{ill|Abe clan|Q11657247|qid=Q11657247}} clan, descendants of Obiko no Mikoto and Takenuma Kawabetsu no Mikoto, is from {{ill|Shimotsuke Province|Q1053699|qid=Q1053699|lt=Shimono}} to Aizu. It was connected to {{ill|Echigo Province|be|Этыго (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئێچیگۆ|cs|Provincie Ečigo|de|Provinz Echigo|es|Provincia de Echigo|fa|ولایت اچیگو|fr|Province d'Echigo|gl|Provincia de Echigo|id|Provinsi Echigo|it|Echigo|ja|越後国|ko|에치고국|lt|Ečigo žemė|nl|Echigo (provincie)|pt|Província de Echigo|ru|Этиго (провинция)|simple|Echigo Province|sk|Ečigo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ечиго|tr|Echigo (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Етіґо|zh|越後國|zh_min_nan|Etigo-kok|zh_yue|越後國|qid=Q666514|lt=Echigo}}, and some point out that there was some historical background to it {{Sfn|Hoga|2013|p=19}}. In addition, in the Aizu region, {{ill|Kamegamori Kofun|Q132363372|qid=Q132363372}} ({{ill|Kawanuma District, Fukushima|Q1155856|qid=Q1155856}}{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Aizu Sakashita Town}}, the second largest in the Tohoku region) and {{ill|Ōtsukayama Kofun|ja|会津大塚山古墳|zh|會津大塚山古墳|qid=Q11381233}}, where {{ill|Triangular-Rimmed Divine Beast Mirror|Q11357232|qid=Q11357232}} was excavated. A large keyhole-shaped tumulus (Q11268718}} was built in the 4th century (early {{ill|Kofun period|Q459939|qid=Q459939}}), which is the fourth largest in the Tohoku region. Archeology has also pointed out that {{ill|Yamato Kingship|Q2658252|qid=Q2658252}} was spread at an early stage.{{Sfn|Hoga|2013|pp=45-49}}.In the Isasumi Shrine's shrine biography, as an extension of the above-mentioned Four Paths Shogun's story, the father and son Obiko-no-Mikoto and Takenuma Kawabetsu-no-Mikoto, who met here, are said to be the ancestors of the nation's development.{{ill|Q813 858|qid=Q813 858|lt=Izanami Shrine (Gods)}} is said to have started with the enshrinement of Izanami no Mikoto}}. For this reason, in the old days, the two deities enshrined were Izanagi no Mikoto and Izami no Mikoto, but at the end of the Edo period, Masafumi Otake, a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Japanese scholar}}, advocated the theory that the two deities were enshrined, Ohiko no Mikoto and Takegawabetsu no Mikoto, and the controversy continued since then {{Sfn|History of Isasumi Shrine|1979|pp=51-54}}. It was after the war that it was decided to enshrine four pillars as it is today {{Sfn|History of Isasumi Shrine|1979|pp=51-54}}. Regarding the divine name ``Isasumi,'' there are theories that it is a transliteration of ``Isanami,'' and that Obiko-no-Mikoto and Takenuma Kawabetsu-no-Mikoto encouraged each other to ``move on,'' but it is not clear {{Sfn|Isasumi (Shinto Dictionary)|1941}}.

=== History ===

=== Founding ===
{{Double image stack|right|Mt. Mikaguradake 0810.JPG|Mt. Hakaseyama 0811.JPG|220|{{center|Top is {{ill|Mount Mikagura|Q11489243|qid=Q11489243}} (Amatsudake),<br />Bottom is {{ill|Mount Hakase|Q11408920|qid=Q11408920}} (left) and Mt. Myojingatake (right)}}{{Small|According to tradition, these are the creation site, second transfer site, and third transfer site of Isasumi deity, respectively. }}}}According to the shrine's legend, in the year 10 of {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}} (10th generation) {{ill|Ōhiko-no-Mikoto|ja|大彦命|zh|大彦命|qid=Q11435420|lt=Obiko no Mikoto}} }Father and son were each dispatched to {{ill|Hokurikudō|Q3139239|qid=Q3139239}} and {{ill|Tōkaidō (region)|Q1196306|qid=Q1196306}} as one of the {{ill|Shidō Shōgun|Q9076804|qid=Q9076804}}, and met in Aizu. After transmitting the agricultural technology and advanced culture of the central region in Aizu, ``Amatsudake'' ({{ill|Mount Mikagura|Q11489243|qid=Q11489243}}, {{Wiki coordinates|37|31|18.67|N|139|25|33.29|E|region:JP-07_type:landmark|location|name=1. {{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagison}}, {{jalink|Izana}, the ancestor god of national land reclamation {{Sfn|History of Isasumi Shrine|1979|p=23}}, it is said that Isasumi Shrine was founded by Mi|Q682306|Isan Takashi}}. After that, '''{{ill|Mount Hakase|Q11408920|qid=Q11408920}}''' ({{Coord|37|21|48.02|N|139|42|53.33|E|region:JP-07_type:landmark|name=2. Dr. Mt.}}), '''Myojingatake''' (Mt. Hasama, {{Wiki coordinates|37|25|40.42|N|139|45|34.68|E|region:JP-07_type:landmark|location|name=3. After passing through Mt. Myojingatake}}), in {{ill|Emperor Kinmei|Q329792|qid=Q329792}}13 ({{ill|552|Q25266|qid=Q25266}}), '''Takada Minamibaru'' (Takamagahara; present-day Ayameen, {{Wiki coordinates|37|27|18.70|N|139|50|24.84|E|region:JP-07_type:landmark|location|name=4. Relocated to Takada Nanbaru (Takamagahara/Iris Garden)}}) {{Sfn|History of Isasumi Shrine|1979|p=23}}. It is said that in the 21st year of Emperor Kinmei ({{ill|560|ab|560|af|560|als|560|am|560 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|560|ar|560|ary|560|ast|560|az|560|azb|۵۶۰ (میلادی)|ban|560|bar|560|be|560|be_x_old|560|bg|560|bn|৫৬০|bpy|মারি ৫৬০|br|560|bs|560.|ca|560|cdo|560 nièng|ceb|560|ckb|٥٦٠|crh|560|cs|560|cv|560|cy|560|da|560|de|560|el|560|eml|560|eo|560|es|560|et|560|eu|560|fa|۵۶۰ (میلادی)|fi|560|fo|560|fr|560|fy|560|ga|560|gan|560年|gd|560|gl|560|he|560|hi|560|hr|560.|ht|560 (almanak jilyen)|hu|560|hy|560|id|560|io|560|it|560|ja|560年|jv|560|ka|560|kk|560 жыл|ko|560년|la|560|lb|560|lij|560|lmo|560|lt|560 m.|map_bms|560|mdf|560|mhr|560|mk|560|mr|इ.स. ५६०|mrj|560 и|ms|560|mzn|۵۶۰|nah|560|nap|560|nds|560|new|सन् ५६०|nl|560|nn|560|no|560|nso|560|oc|560|or|୫୬୦|os|560-æм аз|pl|560|pnb|560|pt|560|qu|560|ro|560|ru|560 год|rue|560|sa|५६०|scn|560|sd|560ع|sh|560.|shn|560|si|560|sk|560|sl|560|sq|560|sr|560|su|560|sv|560|sw|560|tg|Соли 560|th|พ.ศ. 1103|tk|560|tl|560|tly|560|tr|560|tt|560 ел|uk|560|ur|560ء|uz|560|vec|560|vi|560|war|560|wuu|560年|xmf|560|zh|560年|zh_min_nan|560 nî|zh_yue|560年|qid=Q32769}}), the shrine was relocated to its current location '''Takada Higashihara'' and a shrine building was built {{Sfn|History of Isasumi Shrine|1979|p=23}}. During the construction of the shrine, the chief priest was Yoshiki Abe Sukune, a superior, the two middle officials were Kimie Sukune Akayoshi as a plasterer, and Michizane Kuroda Sukune as a plasterer, and a large number of priests, including nine priests and Kengyo, were involved in the service {{Sfn|History of Isasumi Shrine|1979|p=23}}. Among them, Kuroda Sukune is said to be the younger brother of Takenuma Kawabetsu no Mikoto {{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1986}}.According to place name lore, among the mountain names mentioned above, ``Okaguradake'' is said to have been played with {{ill|Kagura|Q1348260|qid=Q1348260}} at the time of its enshrinement, and ``Wakashiyama'' is said to have been named by the Shido Shogun. 24104}} is said to have been derived from the fact that it was called ``Mount Mount'' because people carried it on their waists. Additionally, the {{ill|Okumiya|Q11445659|qid=Q11445659}} of Isasumi Shrine is still enshrined at the third Myojingatake. As mentioned above, the historical reality of the Shido Shogun tale is not clear, but the route from Mt. Mt. Mt. Mt. Mt. Mt. Mt. Mt. Mt. Mt. Mt. Mt. Mt. Mt. Dr. Mt. to Mt. Myojingatake includes the {{ill|Tokonami River|Q106738755|qid=Q106738755}} and {{jalink|Tadami Rivers} from Echigo to Aizu. |Q7674310}} Since the main road is assumed to be along the line, there is a theory that the relocation route of Isasumi Shrine represents the invasion route from Hokuriku by Obiko no Mikoto {{Sfn|Onuma District (Heibonsha)|1993}}. Also, around this route there is a legend of "Sengoku Taro (Sengoku Taro/Sengoku Taro)" who is said to have prevented the relocation of Isasumi Shrine, and it is also pointed out that this legend shows the state of Aizu before its submission to the Yamato kingdom {{Sfn|Onuma County (Heibonsha)|1993}}<ref group="note">According to a legend that remains in Onuma District {{ill|Mishima, Fukushima|Q1205004|qid=Q1205004}}, ``Zenami no Mikoto'' dispatched from the central government tried to move the divine spirit from Amatsudake to Mt. Misaka and Yunowao to Mt. Dr., but on the way, he became hostile to ``Sengoku Taro'' (Sengoku Taro/Sengoku Taro) who was based in Futagoyama. Mikoto divided his army into two parts, Ishigami Pass and Zanbushi Pass, and joined them at Kurosawa, where they fought against Taro, but were defeated ('Ishigami Pass' was named after bringing down a mikoshi, 'Zanbushi Pass' was named after cutting down the enemy, and 'Kurosawa' came from the fact that no one had a hard time). The Army of Life healed its wounds in the hot springs of the gods, prepared its military, and took up a battle position at Sunagohara, but was once again defeated (the name ``Sunagohara'' comes from the fact that Taro Sengoku's men enveloped the Army of Life in a cloud of sand). It is said that Mikoto prepared his weapons at Yuyagisawa, set up camp in Gojojiki, and killed Taro by setting fire on three sides of Futagoyama. It is also said that the place names Zenbazawa and Zennadaira are derived from this Zennami no Mikoto (excerpt from "Mishima Town History", Mishima Town, 1968, pp. 1059-1062). </ref>.

First seen in {{ill|National Histories|Q11420601|qid=Q11420601}} in {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jowa}}10 ({{ill|843|Q23469|qid=Q23469}}) <ref group="Hara" In name="Jowa"/>, the {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} of ``Isasakemijin'' appears to have been promoted from no rank to junior fifth rank lower {{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1986}}.{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extended}} "{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}" established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) {{jalin k|Engishiki Shrine Name Book|Q11064932|Shin Name Book}}, {{ill|Mutsu Province|Q907389|qid=Q907389}}{{ill|Aizu district|de|Aizu-gun|ja|会津郡|qid=Q11381283}} is ``Isasumi Shrine'' It is listed as {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}{{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1986}}. This Aizu County was a county before the separation of Onuma County, and at that time the Aizu region consisted of two counties, Aizu County and {{ill|Yama District, Fukushima|Q1205228|qid=Q1205228}}{{Sfn|Onuma County (Heibonsha)|1993}}. There are three {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shikinai}} shrines in the two districts: Isasumi Shrine and {{ill|Kogaikuni Shrine|ja|蚕養国神社|qid=Q11625493}} (Aizu District), and {{ill|Iwahashi Shrine|Q11587896|qid=Q11587896}} (Yama District), of which only Isasumi Shrine is listed as a Meishin Taisha. Also, as a place name that appears in ``{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Japanese name extract}}'', this place is compared to ``Yashirogo, Aizu District'', but ``Yashiro'' is said to have originated from ``shrine'', that is, Isasumi Shrine {{Sfn|Yashirogo, Aizu District (Heibonsha)|1993}}. In addition, according to "{{ill|Chōya Gunsai|Q11517735|qid=Q11517735}}", in 5 years {{ill|Kōwa (Heian period)|Q1193890|qid=Q1193890}} ({{jalink|1103 As of June 10th, Isasumi Shrine was listed as one of the representative shrines in Mutsu Province.Regarding the above-mentioned Iwaichi Shrine (currently Yama-gun {{ill|Inawashiro|Q669633|qid=Q669633}} Aza Nishimine), in the national history, {{ill|Saikō|Q1324664|qid=Q1324664}}2 ({{ill|855|Q25073|qid=Q25073}})<ref group="original">``Japanese Emperor Montoku's Annals'', 2nd year of Saihira (855), New Year's Day (28th) article. </ref>{{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. In other words, until the mid-9th century, Iwazu Shrine was ranked higher, but in the latter half of the 9th century there was a reversal of shrine status, and by the beginning of the 10th century, when the Engishiki Shinmyocho was compiled, Isasumi Shrine was ranked higher. Regarding this reversal, Iwazu Shrine was ranked high as the {{ill|Kunitsukami|Q60995523|qid=Q60995523}}, which enshrines {{ill|Mount Bandai|Q714605|qid=Q714605}}, while Isasumi Shrine was the central deity at this time, Izananoson.・There is a theory that it was because Izanami no Mikoto was worshiped and ranked as {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Amatsukami}} {{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (gods)|1984}}, and there is also a theory that it was around this time that Shido Shogun was introduced to the auspicious origins of Aizu Takada Town.{{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 1|2001|p=58}}. Furthermore, in the "History of Isasumi Shrine", regarding the relationship between Isasumi Shrine and Iwazui Shrine, in ancient times, Isasumi Shrine established a It is said that there was a complementary relationship in which Iwazu Shrine welcomed Iwazu-no-Kami and enshrined Isa-Sumi-no-Kami as a guest deity.{{Sfn|History of Isasumi Shrine|1979|p=23}}In the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}}, Isasumi Shrine is said to have had the status of {{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379|lt=Ninomiya}} of Mutsu Province {{Sfn|Ichinomiya system in medieval countries|2000|pp=308-309}}. There are few historical materials that tell us about the situation in the medieval period, but the endorsement of ``{{ill|Kokoroshimizu Hachiman Shrine|Q11490593|qid=Q11490593|lt=Todera Hachiman Shrine Nagachō}}'' shows the movement of {{ill|15th century|Q7018|qid=Q7018}}. In addition to the confirmation of the direction of the shrine, {{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1986}}, the reverence of the feudal lord {{ill|Ashina clan (Japan)|Q2975229|qid=Q2975229}} can be seen in several cultural properties that have been passed down to the present day. As for the shrine, it received 300 kanmon from the Ashina clan in the medieval period, and 30 koku from the Matsudaira clan, the lord of the {{ill|Aizu Domain|Q4389944|qid=Q4389944}}, in {{ill|Early modern period|an|Edat Moderna|ar|الحقبة الحديثة المبكرة|ast|Edá Moderna|az|Erkən modern dövr|bar|Friae Neizeid|be|Ранні Новы час|bn|প্রারম্ভিক আধুনিক যুগ|br|Amzerioù modern|ca|Edat moderna|cs|Raný novověk|cy|Cyfnod Modern Cynnar|da|Tidlig moderne tid|de|Frühe Neuzeit|el|Πρώιμη νεότερη περίοδος|eo|Frua moderna epoko|es|Edad Moderna|et|Varauusaeg|eu|Aro Modernoa|fa|دوران نوین آغازین|fi|Varhaismoderni|fr|Époque moderne|gl|Idade Moderna|gn|Ára Ko'ãgagua|he|העת החדשה המוקדמת|hi|प्रारंभिक आधुनिक काल|hu|Korai újkor|ia|Etate Moderne|id|Periode modern awal|io|Modern-epoko|it|Età moderna|ja|近世|kbp|Alɩwaatʊ kɩfatʊ (Période moderne)|ko|근세|ku|Destpêka Dema Nûjen|kw|Oos Arnowydh A-Varr|lb|Neizäit|lfn|Eda moderna|li|Vreugmodernen Tied|lij|Etæ Modèrna|lld|Storia moderna|lmo|Età Modèrna|lo|ຍຸກ​ສະ​ໄຫມ​ຕົ້ນ​|lt|Naujieji amžiai|lv|Agrīnie jaunie laiki|mg|Andro Vaovao|mk|Ран нов век|new|प्रारम्भिक आधुनिक काल|nl|Vroegmoderne tijd|nn|Tidleg nytid|no|Tidlig moderne tid|oc|Edat Modèrna|pap|Edad Moderno|pcd|Histoère modérne|pl|Nowożytność|ps|لومړۍ معاصره دوره|pt|Idade Moderna|rm|Temp modern tempriv|ro|Epoca modernă timpurie|ru|Раннее Новое время|sc|Edade moderna|sh|Rani novi vijek|simple|Early modern period|sq|Periudha e hershme moderne|sr|Rani novi vek|stq|Eermodärne Tied|sv|Tidigmoderna tiden|th|สมัยใหม่ตอนต้น|tl|Makabagong kasaysayan|tr|Yeni Çağ|tt|Иртә яңа заман|uk|Ранній новий період|vi|Thời kỳ cận đại|vls|Nieuwn tyd|wuu|近世|yi|נייע צייט|zh|近世|zh_yue|近代史|qid=Q5308718}}{{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1993}}. Also, there was Kiyotaki-dera Temple, which was founded in {{ill|1339|Q6051|qid=Q6051}} as {{ill|Bettō-ji|Q11396755|qid=Q11396755}}. However, in {{ill|Kanbun (era)|es|Kanbun|fa|کانبون (دوره)|fr|Ère Kanbun|id|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|ko|간분|ru|Камбун (нэнго)|simple|Kanbun (era)|sr|Канбун (ера)|sv|Kanbun|tr|Kanbun (dönem)|zh|寬文|qid=Q1146228}} 7 ({{ill|1667|Q7588|qid=Q7588}}), it was removed from the shrine grounds {{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1986}}.

After that, many shrine buildings were constructed during the {{ill|Kanbun (era)|es|Kanbun|fa|کانبون (دوره)|fr|Ère Kanbun|id|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|ko|간분|ru|Камбун (нэнго)|simple|Kanbun (era)|sr|Канбун (ера)|sv|Kanbun|tr|Kanbun (dönem)|zh|寬文|qid=Q1146228}} years ({{ill|1661|Q7005|qid=Q7005}}-{{ill|1672|Q7614|qid=Q7614}}).

Also, from {{ill|1900|Q2034|qid=Q2034}} (Meiji 33) to {{ill|1916|Q2087|qid=Q2087}} ({{ill|Taishō era|ar|فترة تايشو|br|Oadvezh Taishō|ca|Període Taishō|cs|Období Taišó|de|Taishō-Zeit|eo|Taiŝo-epoko|es|Era Taishō|et|Taishō ajastu|eu|Taishō aroa|fa|دوره تایشو|fi|Taishō-kausi|fr|Ère Taishō|he|תקופת טאישו|hi|ताइशो युग|hu|Taisó-kor|hy|Տայսյո|id|Zaman Taishō|it|Periodo Taishō|ja|大正|ko|다이쇼 시대|lt|Taišio laikotarpis|lv|Taišo periods|ml|തായ്ഷോ കാലഘട്ടം|ms|Zaman Taishō|nl|Taishoperiode|no|Taishō-perioden|pl|Taishō (okres)|pt|Período Taishō|ro|Perioada Taishō|ru|Тайсё|sh|Taishō period|simple|Taishō era|sr|Таишо период|sv|Taishō|th|ยุคไทโช|tl|Panahong Taishō|tr|Taişo Dönemi|uk|Період Тайсьо|uz|Taishō davri|vi|Thời kỳ Đại Chính|zh|大正|zh_classical|大正 (年號)|zh_min_nan|Tāi-chèng|zh_yue|大正 (日本年號)|qid=Q329174}}5), the lord of Aizu {{ jalink|Katayasu Matsudaira|Q569441}} It is known that the second son {{ill|Takeo Matsudaira|Q62085415|qid=Q62085415}} became the chief priest {{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1986}}.After the war, it was listed as {{ill|Beppyo shrine|ja|別表神社|mr|बेप्प्यो तीर्थ|simple|Beppyo shrine|zh|別表神社|qid=Q10898274}} in {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}, and {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|p=518}}, it has been certified as "Shinichi no Miya" by the National Ichinomiya Association in {{ill|Iwashiro Province|Q1370734|qid=Q1370734}}{{ill|Ichinomiya|Q1656379|qid=Q1656379}}. {{ill|2008|Q2004|qid=Q2004}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} On October 3, 2020, the worship hall and shrine were destroyed by a fire, and on October 29 of the same year, the main shrine, kagura hall, shrine offering place, etc. were completely destroyed by fire, so the current main shrine, worship hall, etc. are currently being rebuilt (as of August 2014).

=== God level ===
* {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jowa}}September 5, 10 years ({{ill|843|Q23469|qid=Q23469}}), from no rank to junior fifth rank ("{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}") <ref group="Hara" name="Jowa">Shoku Nihon Koki, September 843, Kotora (5th) article (see {{Harvnb|Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection}}). </ref> - The notation is "Isa Sake Mikami".

The true identity of the treasure The inscription on the round mirror is said to be ``Oshu Ninomiya Shoichi Rank Isasumi Daimyojin, Daido 4th year ({{ill|809|Q30671|qid=Q30671}}) Self-Oldman Yoshikiyo.'' This mirror was burnt down in {{ill|Bunki|Q1324885|qid=Q1324885}}3 ({{ill|1503|Q6141|qid=Q6141}}) and the details are unknown{{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|p=518}}. The Senmei and Iki were also burnt down in this fire, so it is said that in {{ill|Tenbun|Q1192853|qid=Q1192853|lt=Tenbun}} 20th year ({{ill|1551|Q6560|qid=Q6560}}), Sochikyo went to Kyoto and received the Senji and plaque of ``Senior First Rank'', but these were also burnt down later.{{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|p=518}}.

=== Precincts ===

=== Head Office ===
The precincts are 0.66 hectares (20,000 tsubo), consisting of an inner garden of 0.33 hectares (10,000 tsubo) and an outer garden of 0.33 hectares (10,000 tsubo) {{Sfn|History of Isasumi Shrine|1979|p=25}}.

==== Shrine ====
[[File:Isasumi-jinja karishaden.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{Center|Karishaden}}{{Small|Located at the location of the old shrine. }}]]
The main shrine building was destroyed in a fire in {{ill|2008|Q2004|qid=Q2004}} ({{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}}20), so it is currently enshrined in a temporary shrine built on the site of the worship hall.

The old shrine building that was destroyed by fire was built in {{ill|1899|Q7851|qid=Q7851}} ({{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}}32) {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|p=523}}. The old main shrine was Sangensha {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}}, and the old worship hall connected to it by the Heiden had a Shichigensha ryuzukuri copper plate roof {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|p=523}}. The tower gate was built in 1989 ({{ill|1989|Q2425|qid=Q2425}}) and survived the fire mentioned above and still exists today {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|p=523}}. When this tower gate was constructed, the Shinmon gate that had been in use until then was moved to the east (currently the Higashi Shinmon gate) {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|p=523}}.

==== Company collection ====
[[File:Isasumi-jinja, usuzumi-zakura.jpg|thumb|200px|{{Center|Usuzumi-zakura<br />(Aizumisato-cho designated natural monument)}}]]
Because the forest within the shrine grounds was forbidden to enter as a sacred area, a natural forest has been preserved {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|pp=687-688}}. In particular, there are many large trees on the east side along the Miyagawa River, where {{ill|Ulmus davidiana var. japonica|Q844010|qid=Q844010}}, {{ill|Zelkova serrata|Q920344|qid=Q920344}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kitakobushi}}, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Aonaragashiwa}} grow wild. Also, as shrubs, {{ill|Lindera praecox|Q10935819|qid=Q10935819}}, {{ill|Sambucus sieboldiana|Q7409109|qid=Q7409109}}, and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=chimakizasa}}, and as grasses, {{jalink| {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|pp=687-688}}. These vegetations represent the ecology before the settlement of Aizu, and are of botanical and folklore importance, so the shrine bush has been designated as a designated natural monument of Aizu Misato Town {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|pp=687-688}}.Inside Tamagaki, a huge wisteria tree stands to the east of the main shrine ruins. This wisteria grows to a height of about 35 meters or more while wrapping around {{ill|Quercus myrsinifolia|Q1075985|qid=Q1075985}}, etc., and is also called the "flying dragon wisteria" <ref name="Fuji"/><ref name="Explanation board"/>. The tree is said to be over 100 years old and has a root circumference of over 2 meters. Fuji is a giant wisteria tree that is rare in Fukushima Prefecture, and is designated as a natural monument of Fukushima Prefecture. Near this wisteria, there is also a ``Tenkai Sojo hand-planted cypress tree'' that is said to have been planted by {{ill|Tenkai|Q1142310|qid=Q1142310}} in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}}6 ({{ill|1571|Q6666|qid=Q6666}}) as a prayer for healing his mother's illness.<ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|title=Public Relations Aizumisato August issue |number=81 |year=2012 |page=22 |publisher=Aizu Misato Town Public Relations Committee |url=http://www.town.aizumisato.fukushima.jp/resources/content/5479/20130110-150223.pdf |accessdate=2014-10-11 |format=PDF}}</ref>.Near the tower gate stands one of the {{ill|Aizu Gozakura|Q21652321|qid=Q21652321}}, ``''Usuzumizakura'' {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|pp=685-686}}. The scientific name is "Aidus Suzumi" <ref name="Cherry blossom"/>. The petals are double and single, and at first they are white with a hint of ink, but as the season progresses, they turn red. According to the shrine's legend, this tree has been a sacred tree ever since Isasumikami was relocated from Mt. Myojingatake, and every year during the spring flower festival, a banquet is held with rice cakes pounded with this flower in it. This light ink cherry tree is designated as a natural monument of Aizumisato Town <ref name="cherry blossom"/>.In addition, across the road to the south of the precincts is the ``Iris Garden,'' a sacred garden. This area is said to be the site of Takamagahara (Takada Nanbara), where the god Isasumi was first enshrined when he was transferred from Myojingatake. {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History, which is said to have been enshrined for 1 year ({{ill|552|Q25266|qid=Q25266}}-{{ill|560|ab|560|af|560|als|560|am|560 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|560|ar|560|ary|560|ast|560|az|560|azb|۵۶۰ (میلادی)|ban|560|bar|560|be|560|be_x_old|560|bg|560|bn|৫৬০|bpy|মারি ৫৬০|br|560|bs|560.|ca|560|cdo|560 nièng|ceb|560|ckb|٥٦٠|crh|560|cs|560|cv|560|cy|560|da|560|de|560|el|560|eml|560|eo|560|es|560|et|560|eu|560|fa|۵۶۰ (میلادی)|fi|560|fo|560|fr|560|fy|560|ga|560|gan|560年|gd|560|gl|560|he|560|hi|560|hr|560.|ht|560 (almanak jilyen)|hu|560|hy|560|id|560|io|560|it|560|ja|560年|jv|560|ka|560|kk|560 жыл|ko|560년|la|560|lb|560|lij|560|lmo|560|lt|560 m.|map_bms|560|mdf|560|mhr|560|mk|560|mr|इ.स. ५६०|mrj|560 и|ms|560|mzn|۵۶۰|nah|560|nap|560|nds|560|new|सन् ५६०|nl|560|nn|560|no|560|nso|560|oc|560|or|୫୬୦|os|560-æм аз|pl|560|pnb|560|pt|560|qu|560|ro|560|ru|560 год|rue|560|sa|५६०|scn|560|sd|560ع|sh|560.|shn|560|si|560|sk|560|sl|560|sq|560|sr|560|su|560|sv|560|sw|560|tg|Соли 560|th|พ.ศ. 1103|tk|560|tl|560|tly|560|tr|560|tt|560 ел|uk|560|ur|560ء|uz|560|vec|560|vi|560|war|560|wuu|560年|xmf|560|zh|560年|zh_min_nan|560 nî|zh_yue|560年|qid=Q32769}}) Volume 7|1999|pp=526-527}}{{Sfn|History of Isasumi Shrine|1979|p=23}}. Approximately 150 species and 100,000 irises are planted in the garden, and the "Iris Festival" is held from June 15th to July 5th, when these flowers are in full bloom. |url=http://www.aizu-reichi.gr.jp/isasumi/ |accessdate=2014-10-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|Japanese book|title=Iris of Isasumi Shrine (Aizumisato Town) - Fukushima Flower Journey |publisher=Fukushima Minpo |url=http://www.minpo.jp/pub/topics/hanakikou/2014/06/post_327.html | accessdate=2014-10-11}}</ref>.

=== Okumiya ===
'''Okumiya'' is located in Aizu Misato Town Nishimoto Aza Myojindake ({{Coord|37|25|37.26|N|139|45|41.29|E|region:JP-07_type:landmark|name=Okumiya}}), with a stone shrine enshrined on the east side near the summit of Myojingatake.{{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|pp=679-680}}.

The land of Okumiya is said to be the former enshrining place of the god Isasumi, and according to the shrine's legend, the god Isasumi moved from Mt. In the area of ​​Okumiya, a single natural stone was said to be the site of a shrine in ancient times, but in {{ill|Kanpō|de|Kanpō|fa|کانپو|fr|Ère Kanpō|ja|寛保|ko|간포|ru|Кампо (нэнго)|simple|Kanpō|sr|Канпо|sv|Kanpō|tr|Kanpō|zh|寬保|qid=Q1145798}}4 ({{ill|1744|Q7583|qid=Q7583}}), the current 115cm tall stone shrine was built {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|pp=679-680}}.
This Okumiya site is said to indicate that the belief in Isasumi Shrine moved from the mountains to the plains with the development of lowland culture, and has been designated as a designated historical site in Aizumisato Town as the ``Isasumi Shrine Okumiya Site'' {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Vol. 7|1999|pp=679-680}}.

=== Kyougaisha ===
"History of Isasumi Shrine" {{Sfn|History of Isasumi Shrine|1979|p=45}} lists the following 12 shrines as subsidiary shrines outside the precincts.
* Setsusha
** '''Sai Shrine'' - Takada Kamimachi. Regular festival: August 25th.
*Suesha
** Suwa Shrine - Sabugawa. Regular festival: August 27th.
** Rokuyama Shrine - Sparrow Forest. Regular festival: September 1st.
** Godate Kumano Shrine - Sakaino. Regular festival: September 8th.
** Kumano Shrine - Yasuda. Regular festival: September 9th.
** Kasuga Shrine - Okinakata. Regular festival: September 9th.
** Inari Shrine - Akutsu. Regular festival: September 9th.
** Hie Shrine - Shinyashiki. Regular festival: September 9th.
** Inari Shrine - Terasaki. Regular festival: September 19th.
** Ikami Shrine - Sparrow forest. Regular festival: September 29th.
** Ota Shrine - Takada downtown. Regular festival: October 10th of the lunar calendar.
** Hachiman Hakusan Shrine - Saga Segawa. Regular festival: November 9th.

=== Festival ===
<div class="NavFrame" style="width:100%;">
 <div class="NavHead" style="padding:1.5px; line-height:1.7; letter-spacing:1px;">List of annual festivals</div>
 <div class="NavContent" style="text-align:left;">
List of festivals held annually at Isasumi Shrine {{Sfn|History of Isasumi Shrine|1979|pp=43-45}}<ref name="Book of History">Book of History of the Shrine. </ref>. Major festivals and important rituals are shown in bold.
* Every day
** Hikusai (Daily morning)
* Monthly
** Moon Head Festival (1 day)
**Monthly Festival (15th)
* January
** Happo Festival (January 1st)
**Saidan Festival (January 1st) - Middle Festival.
**New Year Festival (January 1st to 7th)
**Genshi Festival (January 3rd) - Middle Festival.
**First Tenjin (January 25th)
*February
**Setsubun Festival (Setsubun Day in February)
** Sesshoseki Inari Shrine Annual Festival/Hatsuuma Festival (first afternoon of February)
** Tenjin Festival (February 25th)
* March
** Plaque commemorative festival (March 15th)
**Vernal Equinox Festival (Vernal Equinox in March)
*April
** Fire Extinguishing Festival (April 15th) - Middle Festival
** Showa Festival (April 29th) - Middle Festival
** Prayer Festival (April 29th) - Grand Festival
**'''Flower Festival''/Daida Kagura (April 29) -Dadai Kagura is an important intangible folk cultural property designated by Aizumisato Town.
* May
**'''Sunayama Festival''' (May 5th (Boys' Festival)) - Middle Festival** Aizu Okunitama Shrine Annual Festival (May 15th)
*June
*Iris Festival (June 15th to July 5th)
*Summer Purification (June 30th)
*July
**'''Rice Planting Festival''' (July 11th to 13th) - Grand festival. Nationally important intangible folk cultural property.
*August
* Sai Shrine Annual Festival (August 24th to 25th)
*September
** Sake Festival (September 1st)
**Lantern Festival (September 2nd)
**'''Reitaisai''' (September 1st to 17th) - Taisai.
** Autumn Equinox Festival (Autumn Equinox Day in September)
* October
** Nukiho Festival (October 9th)
**Kannaho Festival (October 17th) - Middle Festival.
*November
** Meiji Festival (November 3rd) - Middle Festival.
**Hakusan Shrine Annual Festival (November 15th)
**'''Ninamesai'' (November 23rd) - Grand festival.
**Ota Shrine Annual Festival (November 31st)
*December
** Shutenjin (December 25th)
**New Year's Eve Purification, New Year's Eve Festival, Old Shintatsu Burning Festival (December 31st)
</div></div>

Since ancient times in the Aizu region, it has not been easy to find salt, so this is a Shinto ritual in which salt is made as a prayer to avoid being inconvenienced by salt. As a secret passed down from one company to another, the viewing is held in secret.{{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|pp=528-529}}. During the festival, two sand mounds are built in the northeast corner of Tamagaki, and a {{ill|Himorogi|ar|هيموروغي|es|Himorogi|fa|هیموروگی|fi|Himorogi|fr|Himorogi|id|Himorogi|it|Himorogi|ja|神籬|ko|신리 (신토)|pl|Himorogi|pt|Himoragi|ru|Химороги|simple|Himorogi|sv|Himorogi|zh|神籬|qid=Q60587}} is erected on the back sand mound to invite the Aiden deities, Shiogama Okami and Hachiman Okami, and three octagonal stakes and a hammer are placed on the front sand mound {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Vol. 7|1999|pp=528-529}}. Two priests perform the ritual in strange appearances wearing king nose masks and cockscombs {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|pp=528-529}}.

It is a festival ({{ill|Otaue Festival|ja|御田植祭|qid=Q11489226}}) where people pray for a good harvest by performing a simulated rice planting ceremony. Since ancient times, ``the morning rice planting of {{ill|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|qid=Q687168|lt=Ise}}, the afternoon rice planting of Takada, and the evening rice planting of {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|Q482065|qid=Q482065|lt=Atsuta}} {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|pp=529-531}}. There are two types of Otaue Festivals: the pre-celebration type, which is held during the New Year period, and the warm-country type, which is held during the rice-planting season.In the Tohoku region, where rice cultivation has a short history, many Ota-ue Festivals are pre-celebration type.{{Sfn|Otaue Festival (annual event)|2009}}, but perhaps because Aizu opened early, the warm-country type is held at Isasumi Shrine.{{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|pp=652-653}}.: The festival is held after rice planting by general farmers {{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine Otaue Festival (annual event)|2009}}. The festival begins with a Shinko Festival held at the main shrine, followed by young lion chasers going around the town and stirring the muddy fields of Ota Shrine to drive away the boars that are harmful to the rice crops. Afterwards, the mikoshi was carried from the head office to Ota Shrine with a procession of about 200 people. At Ota Shrine, a mikoshi is placed in front of the Goshosaku field, and in front of it {{ill|Saibara|de|Saibara|es|Saibara|fr|Saibara|ja|催馬楽|pl|Saibara|qid=Q1428885}}, rice planting dance, lion dance, and Chigo dance are offered.{{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine Otaue Festival (annual event)|2009}}. The next day, early in the morning, the rice planting in the rice fields is repaired, and the festival ends with the Sanae Festival held at the head office {{Sfn|Isasumi Shrine Rice Planting Festival (annual event)|2009}} This festival, along with the rice planting ritual at Keitoku Inari Shrine} (Kitakata City), has been designated as a national important intangible folk cultural property as the ``Otaue Festival of Aizu.''

=== Cultural assets ===

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
* Vermilion lacquered gold-bronze mikoshi (craft)
*: {{ill|Mikoshi|qid=Mikoshi|lt=Mikoshi}} said to have been created during the {{ill|Muromachi period|Q334845|qid=Q334845}}. It is said that it was dedicated in the year 6 ({{ill|1526|ab|1526|af|1526|als|1526|am|1526 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1526|ar|1526|ary|1526|arz|1526|ast|1526|avk|1526|az|1526|azb|۱۵۲۶ (میلادی)|bar|1526|bcl|1526|be|1526|be_x_old|1526|bg|1526|bn|১৫২৬|bpy|মারি ১৫২৬|br|1526|bs|1526.|ca|1526|cdo|1526 nièng|ce|1526 шо|ceb|1526|ckb|١٥٢٦|crh|1526|cs|1526|cv|1526|cy|1526|da|1526|de|1526|diq|1526|el|1526|eml|1526|eo|1526|es|1526|et|1526|eu|1526|fa|۱۵۲۶ (میلادی)|fi|1526|fo|1526|fr|1526|frr|1526|fur|1526|fy|1526|ga|1526|gan|1526年|gcr|1526|gd|1526|gl|1526|he|1526|hi|१५२६|hr|1526.|ht|1526 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1526|hy|1526|ia|1526|id|1526|ilo|1526|io|1526|is|1526|it|1526|ja|1526年|jv|1526|ka|1526|kaa|1526|kk|1526 жыл|ko|1526년|krc|1526 джыл|la|1526|lb|1526|lfn|1526|lij|1526|lmo|1526|lt|1526 m.|lv|1526. gads|mai|१५२६|map_bms|1526|mdf|1526|mg|1526|mhr|1526|mi|1526|min|1526|mk|1526|mn|1526 он|mr|इ.स. १५२६|mrj|1526 и|ms|1526|my|၁၅၂၆|nah|1526|nap|1526|nds|1526|nds_nl|1526|new|सन् १५२६|nl|1526|nn|1526|no|1526|nrm|1526|nso|1526|oc|1526|or|୧୫୨୬|os|1526-æм аз|pl|1526|pnb|1526|pt|1526|qu|1526|ro|1526|ru|1526 год|rue|1526|sa|१५२६|sah|1526|scn|1526|sd|1526ع|se|1526|sh|1526.|shn|1526|simple|1526|sk|1526|sl|1526|smn|1526|sq|1526|sr|1526|su|1526|sv|1526|sw|1526|ta|1526|te|1526|tg|Соли 1526|th|พ.ศ. 2069|tk|1526|tl|1526|tly|1526|tr|1526|tt|1526 ел|uk|1526|ur|1526ء|uz|1526|vec|1526|vi|1526|vls|1526|wa|1526|war|1526|wuu|1526年|xmf|1526|yi|1526|zh|1526年|zh_min_nan|1526 nî|zh_yue|1526年|qid=Q6325}}) by the father and son Moriyasu and Moritsune Ashina, the owners of the Takada mansion. The roof is clad in Hogai-zo copper plates, and the pillars are made of gilt bronze. The front door is painted with vermilion lacquer and has the gilt bronze emblems of ``Kenfutsubiki'' and ``Samitsu Tomoe'' on it, and on three sides other than the front, there are copper plates with the gilt bronze wheel treasure crest engraved on them, and a perimeter surrounds them. The parapets around the perimeter are made of gilt bronze, and there are stairs and gilt bronze torii gates on all sides. This mikoshi has the characteristics of the late Muromachi period, and is considered to be an excellent item from the same period.
*: Currently stored and exhibited in the treasure hall of Isasumi Shrine. Designated on July 3, 1945 <ref> [http://www.town.aizumisato.fukushima.jp/11,5774,176.html List of nationally designated cultural properties] (Aizumisato Town homepage). </ref><ref name="Nationally designated">{{Nationally designated cultural properties database|201|5173|Vermilion lacquer gold bronze mikoshi}}</ref>.

* Important cultural property (tangible cultural property)
** 1 pair of wooden guardian dogs (craft)
**: A pair of {{ill|Komainu|ar|كوماينو|as|কোমাইনু|de|Komainu|et|Komainu|fa|کومااینو|fr|Komainu|hu|Komainu|ja|狛犬|ko|코마이누|pl|Komainu|pt|Komainu|ru|Комаину|simple|Komainu|sq|Komainu|zh|狛犬|qid=Q20155846}} estimated to have been created during the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|ar|فترة نانبوكو تشو|bg|Нанбоку-чо|bn|নান্‌বোকু-চোও যুগ|ca|Període Nanboku-chō|cs|Období Nanbokučó|de|Namboku-chō|es|Período Nanbokuchō|eu|Nanboku-chō Aroa|fa|دوره نانبوکوچو|fi|Nanboku-chō-kausi|fr|Époque Nanboku-chō|he|תקופת שתי החצרות הקיסריות|hu|A japán császári udvar különválása|id|Zaman Nanboku-chō|it|Periodo Nanboku-chō|ja|南北朝時代 (日本)|ko|남북조 시대 (일본)|ms|Tempoh Nanboku-chō|nl|Nanboku-cho-periode|pt|Período Nanboku-chō|ru|Период Намбокутё|simple|Nanboku-chō period|sr|Нанбокућо период|sv|Nanboku-chō|th|ยุคราชสำนักเหนือ-ใต้|tr|Nanboku-chō Dönemi|uk|Період Намбокутьо|vi|Nam–Bắc triều (Nhật Bản)|zh|南北朝时代 (日本)|zh_min_nan|Nanboku-tyô sî-tāi|zh_yue|南北朝 (日本)|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanbokucho period}}. Each one is 97 centimeters in height, and is a rare giant wooden guardian dog in Japan. The statue is made of marquetry and painted with lacquer. It has a small head and a large body, and is different from those popular in the Heian and Kamakura periods {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|pp=650-651}}. It is currently stored and displayed in the Treasure Hall. Designated on October 1, 1952 <ref name="prefectural designation"> [http://www.town.aizumisato.fukushima.jp/11,5776,176.html List of prefectural designated cultural properties] (Aizumisato Town homepage). </ref>.

=== Cultural property designated by Aizumisato Town ===
* Important cultural property (tangible cultural property)
** 1 golden door (craft)
**: A golden door that appears to have been made during the Muromachi period. The size is 161.8 cm in length, 55 cm in width, and 3.8 cm in thickness. The door is smaller but more luxurious than the ancient door, and it is presumed that it was originally the door of the main shrine. It is inconceivable that this door could have been made solely by the efforts of commoners and believers, and it is pointed out that there was a great deal of support from the feudal lord. In ancient documents, the shrine building was burnt down in {{ill|Bunki|Q1324885|qid=Q1324885}}3 ({{ill|1503|Q6141|qid=Q6141}}), and in {{ill|Eishō (Muromachi period)|Q1193577|qid=Q1193577}}11 ({{jalink|1514 It appears that the shrine was rebuilt by father and son {{ill|Moriji Ashina|Q11625151|qid=Q11625151}} and {{ill|Moriji|Q11625149|qid=Q11625149|lt=Moriji}} in the year |Q6204}}, and this door is presumed to have been created at that time. The shrine building was also burnt down in {{ill|Tenmei|Q1194121|qid=Q1194121}} 3rd year ({{ill|1783|Q7745|qid=Q7745}}), but it seems that the shrine survived the disaster {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|pp=661-662}}. It is currently stored and displayed in the Treasure Hall. Designated on March 1, 1970 <ref name="Town Designated"> [http://www.town.aizumisato.fukushima.jp/11,5775,176.html List of Town Designated Cultural Properties] (Aizumisato Town Home Page). </ref>.
** 1 ancient door (craft)**: A door that appears to have been made during the Muromachi period. It is a gilt-bronze door made of red lacquer with a camellia pattern, and measures 173 centimeters in length, 49.5 centimeters in width, and 6 centimeters in thickness. It is presumed that the door was originally used in the inner sanctum of the main shrine. Like the Golden Door, this door was rebuilt in 1514, and is thought to have survived the fire in 1783. {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|p=662}} It is currently stored and displayed in the Treasure Hall. Designated on March 1, 1972 <ref name="Town Designation"/>.
** 1 pair of Tekka tables (craft)
**: Iron {{ill|Huabiao|Q1135870|qid=Q1135870}} (meaning {{ill|Torii|Q234731|qid=Q234731}}). It is cylindrical and hollow inside, with a total length of 193 cm and a circumference of 196 cm. According to "Aizu old affairs miscellaneous notes", it is said to have been built by a man named Nagamine Ecchu on October 26, {{ill|Meiō|Q1193841|qid=Q1193841}} first year ({{ill|1492|Q6679|qid=Q6679}}), and it has both pillars but no rainbow beam. It is also mentioned in "{{ill|Shinpen Aizu Fudoki|Q11503941|qid=Q11503941}}", and from these documents it is assumed that it is a tube used to insert the legs of a torii gate. On the other hand, there is also a legend that these are the pillars left after the lanterns were broken {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|pp=664-665}}. Designated on April 1, 1994 <ref name="Town designation"/>.
** Japanese Kisho Banquet Waka Volume 1 (ancient document)**: {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, {{ill|Waka (poetry)|Q737148|qid=Q737148}} in ink and paper. Total length 5.5 meters. The foreword is written by Ankyu Hattori, the waka poem is written by {{ill|Yoshikawa Koretari|Q4053782|qid=Q4053782}}, and the afterword is written by Kiyoo Mizuno. On August 17, {{ill|Kanbun (era)|es|Kanbun|fa|کانبون (دوره)|fr|Ère Kanbun|id|Kanbun (era)|ja|寛文|ko|간분|ru|Камбун (нэнго)|simple|Kanbun (era)|sr|Канбун (ера)|sv|Kanbun|tr|Kanbun (dönem)|zh|寬文|qid=Q1146228}}10 ({{ill|1670|Q7606|qid=Q7606}}), the lord of Aizu, {{ill|Hoshina Masayuki|Q837236|qid=Q837236}}, became a vassal and a priest. This is a collection of waka poems that were composed about the contents of the lecture at a banquet (shokuen) held when Ankyū Hattori held a lecture on the ``{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935|lt=Nihonki}} Jindai Scrolls'' by Ankyū Hattori, who gathered 42 people, including 42 people, in the castle grounds. At this time, 42 people were reciting waka and one person was reciting {{ill|Shi (poetry)|Q1759242|qid=Q1759242}}{{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|pp=666-667}}. Designated on March 1, 1972 <ref name="Town Designation"/>.
* Important intangible folk cultural property
** Taidai Kagura - Designated on March 25, 1975 <ref name="Town designation"/>.
* Historic sites
** Isasumi Shrine Okumiya area - Designated on June 20, 1964 <ref name="Town designation"/>.
* Natural monument** Usuzokuzakura - Designated on April 1, 1972 <ref name="Town Designation"/>. Registered as a Fukushima Prefecture Green Cultural Property on September 13, 1981.<ref name="Cherry Blossoms">{{PDFlink|[http://www.town.aizumisato.fukushima.jp/resources/content/7628/20091118-154026.pdf Usuzumi Sakura]}} (Aizumisato Town Home Page). </ref>.
** Isasumi Shrine Shrine - Designated April 1, 1994 <ref name="Town Designation"/>. Registered as a Fukushima Prefecture Green Cultural Property on September 13, 1981. </ref>.

'''Attached facilities''
* Treasure Hall - Exhibits vermilion lacquered gold bronze mikoshi (Important Cultural Property), wooden guardian dogs, etc.
** Opening hours: 9am - 4pm
** Admission fee: 300 yen for adults/150 yen for children under 18 years old

'''Access'''
* Railway: {{ill|East Japan Railway Company|ar|شركة شرق اليابان للسكك الحديدية|arz|شركة سكك حديد شرق اليابان|az|Şərqi Yaponiya dəmiryol şirkəti|azb|دوغو ژاپون دمیریول‌لاری|bcl|Kompanya nin Agihang-riles sa Subangang Hapon|ca|Companyia de Ferrocarrils del Japó Oriental|cs|JR East|da|East Japan Railway Company|de|East Japan Railway Company|eo|JR Orienta|es|East Japan Railway Company|fa|شرکت راه‌آهن شرق ژاپن|fi|JR Higashi-Nihon|fr|East Japan Railway Company|hu|East Japan Railway Company|hy|East Japan Railway Company|id|Perusahaan Kereta Api Jepang Timur|it|East Japan Railway Company|ja|東日本旅客鉄道|jv|East Japan Railway Company|ko|동일본여객철도|ms|Syarikat Kereta Api Jepun Timur|nds|JR Oostjapan|nl|East Japan Railway Company|pl|East Japan Railway Company|pt|East Japan Railway Company|ru|East Japan Railway Company|simple|East Japan Railway Company|sv|JR Higashi Nihon|th|บริษัทรถไฟญี่ปุ่นตะวันออก|tl|East Japan Railway Company|tr|East Japan Railway Company|uk|East Japan Railway Company|ur|ایسٹ جاپان ریلوے کمپنی|vi|Công ty Đường sắt Đông Nhật Bản|wuu|东日本旅客铁道|zh|東日本旅客鐵道|zh_yue|東日本旅客鐵道|qid=Q499071}} (JR East) {{ill|Tadami Line|Q1054717|qid=Q1054717}} {{ill|Aizu-Takada Station|Q4699459|qid=Q4699459}} (approximately 25 minutes walk) - 7 trains a day (only 1 train both up and down between 11:00 and 16:00).
* Bus: From {{ill|Aizu-Wakamatsu Station|Q4699462|qid=Q4699462}} Aizu Bus: {{ill|Aizu Bus|Q11381220|qid=Q11381220|lt=bound for Nagaino}} and get off at "Yokomachi" bus stop (about 40 minutes on board, 3 minutes' walk after getting off) - About 1-2 buses per hour during the day.
* By car: Parking available <ref>[https://isasumi.or.jp/access.html Access information] Isasumi Shrine Viewed on November 20, 2023</ref>

'''Surroundings'''
* Monjudo Hall - Originally located within the grounds of Isasumi Shrine as ``Okunoin'' {{Sfn|Aizu Takada Town History Volume 7|1999|pp=518-519}}.
